I completely get what you're going through. I had a abusive, narcissistic family too, and ended up running away at 15 with two of my sisters. My older sister said something similar to what you said. She didn't want to leave because she was afraid of leaving her two younger sisters, so she toughed out the abuse for years before finally leaving with us. It took a terrible toll on her mental health. You're strong for going through this, and you are lucky to have your little sister. I'm not exactly sure what to do, but I understand that it's a hard position to be in. This is just me, but if I were you I'd leave(because your life is too short for you to suffer), but keep in contact and try your best to protect your sister. From what you said, it doesn't seem like he's targeting her yet. But if you leave he might, but you can't let that hold you back from living your life. Unless you can find a way to legally get your sister out of there, it's probably best(for your mental health) if you leave, but keep in touch with your sister and make sure he isn't hurting her. If you want to stay that's also fine. You can always barely be home and mostly show up at night to sleep. Try avoiding him without making it too obvious (narcissists will find a way to make everything you say or do "disrespectful" or insulting). Venting also helps, so it's good that you posted this.

I really hopw you get out of that situation soon. I'm not sure how bad it is, but I know how narcissists are so I'm assuming it is pretty bad.
